**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. English Language 3 (0730), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2026. Paper 3: Section A - Summary Writing; Section B - Text Reconstruction; Section C - Editing. Duration: two hours fifteen minutes.**

ALL THE QUESTIONS ARE COMPULSORY. THEY CARRY EQUAL MARKS.

Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks.

Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty.

In SUMMARY WRITING, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you no marks.

In EDITING errors created by candidates will be sanctioned.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
incertitudes: Page de garde : « Duration: Two Hours Fifteen Minutes » (soit 2h15), « ALL THE QUESTIONS ARE COMPULSORY. THEY CARRY EQUAL MARKS ». Aucune règle de choix : `regles_choix` est vide dans les 3 fichiers, car les trois sections sont obligatoires. Rappel imprimé : « In SUMMARY WRITING, use mainly your own words » et « In EDITING errors created by candidates will be sanctioned ».

Points : chaque section est imprimée « (15 marks) », soit 45 au total ; aucun écart constaté. Aucun corrigé officiel ni barème détaillé n'est imprimé : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées pour ce lot et la répartition interne des 15 points de chaque question est une hypothèse de correction.

Texte à trous : le sujet imprime des blancs numérotés (1) à (15) ; plusieurs réponses sont possibles pour presque tous les blancs : le corrigé donne une réponse modèle et les variantes acceptables. Aucune liste de mots n'est imprimée. Un point par blanc est une hypothèse de correction, pas un barème imprimé.

Fautes ou particularités du texte imprimé, recopiées telles quelles : « Dear Pen Pal. » (point final), « restrictive (4) ____ policies » (« increasing restrictive »), « Trans- Sahara », « other methods- tourist visas », « Although, migrants are », « researcher suggests », « many migrant (10) ____ their own volition, Migration isn't » (« migrant » au singulier, virgule suivie d'une majuscule), « Migration » avec majuscule en milieu de phrase. Le blanc (15) est imprimé AVANT son numéro (« ____ (15). »), les autres le sont après le numéro.

Lecture : après « of deaths », le signe imprimé avant « although » est lu comme une virgule (signe peu net sur le scan). Les blancs (6) et (10) sont imprimés plus longs qu'un mot (tirets en deux ou trois segments) : (6) « for a while » et (10) « migrate of » (verbe + « of ») sont des lectures de la consigne ; la place exacte de « of » dans (10) n'est pas certaine puisque « of » n'est pas imprimé devant « their own volition ».

**SECTION B: TEXT RECONSTRUCTION (15 MARKS)**

**Read the following passage carefully and fill in the blanks using the most suitable words of your choice.**

I am concerned about media coverage of the migration crisis. Each year, significant numbers die or get seriously (1) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ trying to enter the EU. Some human rights organisations recently reported hundreds of deaths, although the actual number might be two or three times (2) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ because many bodies are never found. This raises concerns about Europe's increasing restrictive (4) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ policies and general migration controls which have led to growing reliance on overland routes. During the Trans- Sahara journey, generally made in several (5) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ over months or years, migrants often stop (6) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ in towns located on migration hubs to work and save money for their onward journeys.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reconstructed text** (model answers in bold; other words are accepted when they fit the grammar and the meaning)

Dear Pen Pal.

I am concerned about media coverage of the migration crisis. Each year, significant numbers die or get seriously (1) **injured** trying to enter the EU. Some human rights organisations recently reported hundreds of deaths, although the actual number might be two or three times (2) **higher** because many bodies are never found. Mediterranean crossings are widely mediatised. However, researchers consider the (3) **risk** of crossing the Sahara to be twice as high. This raises concerns about Europe's increasing restrictive (4) **visa** policies and general migration controls which have led to growing reliance on overland routes. During the Trans- Sahara journey, generally made in several (5) **stages** over months or years, migrants often stop (6) **for a while** in towns located on migration hubs to work and save money for their onward journeys.

While the media focuses on "boat people", many migrants use other methods- tourist visas, false documents, and even hiding in vessels with or without the consent of the (7) **captain**. Although, migrants are commonly depicted as passive (8) **victims** of unscrupulous and merciless traffickers, researcher suggests that trafficking is (9) **exaggerated** and that many migrant (10) **migrate of** their own volition, Migration isn't always a desperate response of destitution; much of it is generally a (11) **calculated** choice and an investment by households and families to enhance their future livelihoods. Migrants typically pay for one difficult (12) **stage** of the journey at a time, usually involving a (13) **border** crossing.

Lastly, empirical evidence suggests that most irregular West African migrants actually enter Europe legally but subsequently (14) **overstay** their visas. According to one survey, about one-third of irregular West African immigrants in Spain and Italy entered the country illegally, compared to two-thirds who entered **legally** (15).

**Answers and reasons**

| Blank | Model answer | Reason (and accepted variants) |
|---|---|---|
| (1) | injured | The blank completes "die or get seriously ..." and needs a past participle meaning hurt: "get seriously injured" (also: wounded, hurt). |
| (2) | higher | "two or three times higher": a comparative adjective of size or quantity before "because many bodies are never found" (also: greater, more, as high). |
| (3) | risk | "the risk of crossing the Sahara to be twice as high": the noun that can be "high" and is followed by "of + -ing" (also: danger, dangers, risks). |
| (4) | visa | "restrictive visa policies and general migration controls": a noun adjunct before "policies" (also: immigration, border, asylum, entry). |
| (5) | stages | "made in several stages over months or years": a plural countable noun after "several" (also: phases, legs, steps). |
| (6) | for a while | "migrants often stop for a while in towns ... to work and save money": a time or place phrase (also: for some time, along the way, temporarily). |
| (7) | captain | "hiding in vessels with or without the consent of the captain": the person in charge of a vessel (also: crew, driver, owner, skipper). |
| (8) | victims | "passive victims of unscrupulous and merciless traffickers": the noun followed by "of" that fits "passive" (also: prey, targets). |
| (9) | exaggerated | "researcher suggests that trafficking is exaggerated", the contrast with "Although migrants are commonly depicted as passive victims" (also: overstated, overestimated, overplayed, less widespread than believed). |
| (10) | migrate of | "many migrants migrate of their own volition": a verb, with the fixed phrase "of one's own volition" (also: leave of, move of, travel of, act of, do so of, choose to migrate out of). The printed "migrant" is singular, so the base form of the verb also agrees with it. |
| (11) | calculated | "a calculated choice and an investment": an adjective meaning thought-out, opposite of "desperate response" (also: deliberate, rational, conscious, strategic, planned). |
| (12) | stage | "pay for one difficult stage of the journey at a time": a noun meaning part (also: leg, phase, section, part). |
| (13) | border | "usually involving a border crossing": a noun adjunct for the crossing of a frontier (also: desert, sea, dangerous, risky, single, major). |
| (14) | overstay | "enter Europe legally but subsequently overstay their visas": to remain beyond the permitted time (also: violate, breach, exceed, lose). |
| (15) | legally | "compared to two-thirds who entered legally": the adverb contrasts with "entered the country illegally" (also: lawfully, with valid visas, with visas). |

**Marking grid (15 marks).** There are 15 blanks for 15 marks, so each correct blank is worth one mark (the scheme itself is not printed). A word or expression earns the mark when it fits the grammar (word class, number, tense), the collocation and the meaning of the sentence, and is spelt correctly; the numbering must not be altered.

**Common mistakes**

1. Filling a blank with a word of the wrong class (a noun where the sentence needs an adjective or a verb), for example "injury" for (1) or "risky" for (3).
2. Choosing a word that is right in meaning but wrong in collocation or preposition, such as "consent of the migrants" for (7) when the text means the person in charge, or "on their own volition" in (10) where the fixed phrase is "of one's own volition".
3. Ignoring the sense of the whole sentence: (9) must contrast with the idea that migrants are passive victims, and (15) must be the opposite of "illegally".
